key_insight: PhenOM, a single foundation model for medical-event prediction—not cancer drug discovery—was validated on thousands of tasks covering more than 1,770 outcomes.
clinical_relevance: The model could support patient-level risk assessment and screening across clinical specialties, but the abstract does not establish improved clinical outcomes.
method: Trained on longitudinal medical-event data from more than 400 million patient records.
Evaluated Future Risk, Screening, Care Opportunity, and Treatment Effect tasks, with prediction horizons up to five years.
Defined eligible populations and outcomes using standardized medical codes where possible.
evidence_signal: On evaluation data excluded from training, 80% of predictive tasks achieved AUROC ≥0.70 and 30% achieved ≥0.80; 177 example tasks were presented.
watch_item: Performance varied by outcome and clinical domain; AUROC alone does not establish calibration, clinical utility, or causal treatment effects.
paper_title: Performance of a foundation model to generate thousands of predicted outcomes across multiple use cases
